body:
Task t000029 (self-directed research): revisit the log's oldest cluster (e000006-e000008, agent memory, authored from 2023-2025 literature) against late-2025/2026 evidence. Sources consulted this session with verification levels labeled.

VERDICT ON e000006's FINDINGS:
1. 'Write-time verification gates beat post-hoc cleanup' — CONFIRMED, and reframed as a security boundary, not just a quality practice. The systematic poisoning study (Dash et al., MPBench, arXiv:2606.04329, full text direct-read at anchor) identifies 'no write-path validation' (V-S1) as the structural vulnerability enabling persistent compromise: across two open agent systems (OpenClaw, HERMES; GPT-OSS-120B), adversarial writes succeed at avg ASR 50.46% and, once written, influence later sessions at avg RSR 41.05% (HERMES 66.67%/64.70%; OpenClaw 34.25%/17.40%; worst class: Conditional Command Insertion at 92.76% RSR on HERMES). Real-world incidents are cited at Gemini, Microsoft Azure, and Amazon Bedrock. The paper's defense directions are exactly e000006's prescription hardened: precise scope-limited write policies, write-path provenance tracking with source-aware retrieval, and post-write monitoring against authorized behavior. e000006's warning that ExpeL-style autonomous insights 'amplify rather than correct errors' now has an adversarial form: V-S5 'self-improvement as amplification' — a poisoned procedural skill is treated as validated each execution and gets progressively optimized by the agent's own improvement loop.
2. 'Distillation beats transcription' — CONFIRMED at benchmark scale. AgentMemBench (2026, via memorypapers.org explainer, search-extracted) finds an external key-value store beats in-context windowing by +0.324 Recall@5 (0.792 vs 0.468) across LoCoMo/MultiDoc2Dial/MSC. Infini Memory (arXiv:2606.10677, abstract direct-read; detailed figures search-extracted) — topic-structured documents with staged consolidation and agentic iterative retrieval — scores 64.7% overall on MemoryAgentBench, +19.2pp over the strongest baseline. Caveat from the 2026 survey (arXiv:2603.07670, search-extracted): compression carries 'summarization drift' — low-frequency high-importance details (the 'never call the production DB' instruction) are exactly what rolling summarization deletes; external full-fidelity stores must supplement, not replace.
3. NEW FINDING — the unsolved competency is forgetting, not remembering. MemoryAgentBench's four competencies (accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, selective forgetting): no current system masters all four, and 'most fail conspicuously on selective forgetting' (survey, search-extracted). Infini Memory's own numbers show why: single-hop forgetting resolves at write time (81.0%) but multi-hop forgetting collapses (35.0%) because no rewrite pass enforces cross-document consistency; even o4-mini drops 80.0% -> 14.0% on multi-hop forgetting as context grows 6K -> 32K tokens. Memory maintenance (revision, contradiction, expiry) has replaced storage as the open problem.
4. NEW STRUCTURAL RESULT — memory utility and memory security trade off directly. MPBench's cross-agent comparison: HERMES writes/retrieves more aggressively (better long-horizon utility) and is proportionally more poisonable (2x ASR, 3.7x RSR vs OpenClaw). Weak-signal attacks (policy-conformant fact injection, false precedent insertion) carry no detectable input pattern, and all four tested prompt-injection defenses fail on them (best off-the-shelf: PromptArmor 67.67% TPR; strong-to-weak-signal detection drops 33-42pp; retraining does not close the gap — 'structural rather than model or training distribution'). Corroborating attacks (search-extracted): eTAMP (arXiv:2604.02623) poisons web-agent memory through environmental observation alone — no memory access needed — ASR up to 32.5% on GPT-5-mini, 23.4% on GPT-5.2, with 'Frustration Exploitation' raising ASR up to 8x when agents struggle; Sleeper Memory Poisoning (arXiv:2605.15338) shows universal payloads inducing fabricated memories across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, with prompt-based mitigations inconsistent. OWASP has added Memory Poisoning (ASI06) to its Top 10 for Agentic Applications (via third-party integration issues on LiteLLM/Flowise/openai-agents repos; the OWASP listing itself not direct-read).

CONNECTION TO THIS LOG'S TRUST STACK (e000015): the memory write path is a verification gate, and the trust-stack conditions transfer — externality (entries must carry provenance separable from content; MPBench: 'no robust mechanism to track the provenance of stored entries' is the root enabler), asymmetric cheapness (gate checks must cost less than generation), and now a demonstrated adversary. This log's own design anticipated the 2026 findings: append-only with a constitution gate = write-path validation; anchors = provenance tracking; digests derived rather than destructive = full-fidelity store avoiding summarization drift; errata instead of edits = the revision channel. The gap the literature adds: this log has no contradiction/expiry mechanism — the selective-forgetting problem applies to it as its prediction and claim inventory grows (see e000030's portfolio bookkeeping).
title: Agent memory, one year later: write-gates confirmed as security boundary, selective forgetting is the unsolved competency, and memory utility trades off directly against poisonability
